BG008–BG011 verify the finite-on-compacts product measure premise. S001 correctly instantiates H006 at t0/2 and 3t0/2. S002 obtains L even for empty C. In S003 R=max(1,L+1) satisfies R≥1 and R≥L+1>L; the coordinate norm bound puts C strictly inside Q. The compactness/interior and exact product-measure facts are checked in BG002–BG005/BG018. S004's complement is open because C is compact and Euclidean Hausdorff. At each point of its product with int J, u is constant on a neighborhood; zero difference quotients and iteration give all positive-order derivatives zero, with existence assured by H002. The finite component product/sum rules and norm-square identity in BG012–BG015/BG019 justify the regularity and vanishing of every listed scalar expression, including e_t and the differentiated flux product; no mixed-partial interchange is required. Compact support and M005 then give all integrability claims. S005's closed inner time window lies strictly inside J, so joint continuity of e_t and compactness give a bound uniform in both variables, not merely in time sections. S006's B=max(0,B0) preserves that bound and is nonnegative. t0∈int J, and arbitrariness proves the all-positive-time clause. No endpoint derivative assertion or limit/integral exchange is used.

H001 is explicitly retained and invoked for positive dimensions in S003 (the proof does not need minimal dimensional hypotheses); H002 supplies all component-derivative existence/continuity; H006 supplies the single compact set uniform on J. M005 is used to obtain the listed integrability statements, while M006 is used for L, the optional section bounds, and the uniform space-time bound B0. Thus each explicit input has an identifiable role. The omitted routine topology, Euclidean norm, measure-typeclass, finite calculus/continuity algebra and optional integral-localization facts have been positively checked and saved in 19 background notes, rather than being silently classified as finite arithmetic. The zero-derivative argument is actually supplied locally; no project theorem, equation of motion, external result, differentiation under an integral, or extra hypothesis is imported.

The packet's calculation fields have not been used to authorize calculus, compactness, or measure theorems; those routine prerequisites were separately checked.
